## Setting
Dividing the utility bills. The five people in a shared house have been splitting gas, water, and electricity in a way that was agreed when only three of them lived there. They are deciding how the bills will be divided from now on. Participants: May, Daisuke, Servas, Minato and Midori. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Electrician's quote for the rooms
- The last twelve utility statements
- Monthly settle observed at another house
- Trial run of a reconciliation template
- Kitchen notice about the cooler
- Winter habits at a house paying ahead
- Plug-in monitor readings room by room
- Sunlight and heating need by room
- Payment log for the last twelve months
- Settling up when the last rooms filled

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Servas, Midori, Minato, May and Daisuke. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. | Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |

Name: May
Age: 24
Gender: female
Personality: May is a confident, sociable woman with a playful side. She is charming to those around her and often plays the role of entertainer. Name: Daisuke
Age: 16
Gender: male
Personality: Daisuke is very introverted and cautious, and tends to be somewhat passive when interacting with others. He finds it difficult to express his feelings and thoughts to others, and often struggles with his emotions internally. Name: Servas
Age: 85
Gender: male
Personality: Servas has a very calm and composed personality. Based on the knowledge and experience he has gained over the years, he often gives advice to those around him. Name: Minato
Age: 10
Gender: male
Personality: Minato has a calm personality and likes to interact with people around him in a peaceful manner. He is highly sensitive and sensitive to the feelings of others, but he is not good at asserting himself and sometimes has difficulty expressing his opinions.

Name: Midori
Age: 38
Gender: female

- B: Seasonal Fixed Rate. A set monthly figure is agreed in advance for each season, and the difference against the actual bills is settled once at the end of the year.
- C: Flat Household Share. The total is divided by the number of residents each month, with the amount recalculated whenever someone moves in or out of the house.

- Electrician's quote for the rooms: An electrician came to look and quoted 34,000 yen a room to fit sub-meters, plus a 3,000 yen check on each every year and two days of wiring.

- Trial run of a reconciliation template: A year-end reconciliation template trialled on the house's own figures meant keying in every invoice from the year one by one, then computing five refunds or top-ups separately.
- Kitchen notice about the cooler: A notice about the cooler went up in the house's kitchen in July and stayed all summer; two people said they sweated it out rather than have a pooled bill argued over.
- Winter habits at a house paying ahead: In a household paying a figure fixed ahead for each season, nobody prices a switch before flicking it; they said the hall heater simply stayed on through January.
- Plug-in monitor readings room by room: A plug-in monitor moved between the rooms, a week in each, found the heaviest drawing roughly four times the lightest, most of that a heater and a desktop left running.
- Sunlight and heating need by room: Two of the five rooms take no direct sun and need heat from November, while the south pair stay warm into December; the rooms were originally handed out by lot.
- Payment log for the last twelve months: The house's payment log shows three of the last twelve months settled more than a fortnight late, each time after somebody queried why the amount asked of them had moved again.
- Settling up when the last rooms filled: When the last two rooms filled up mid-month, it took three weeks to agree what the newcomers owed for the days before they arrived, and part was written off.

## Setting
Dividing the utility bills. The five people in a shared house have been splitting gas, water, and electricity in a way that was agreed when only three of them lived there. They are deciding how the bills will be divided from now on. Participants: May, Daisuke, Servas, Minato and Midori. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.

- Settling up when the last rooms filled

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Servas, Midori, Minato, May and Daisuke. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the options | 4 turns | every participant votes; the option with the most votes is adopted |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied options is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.
